Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Can someone sincere be wrong about hearing God?

Yes, and honesty alone cannot rule it out. List explanations, ask what each predicts, and see which survive.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ٤٠ وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ٤١ وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ٤٢ تَنزِيلٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ٤٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

[That] indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the word of a noble Messenger. And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember. [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

Quran · Al-Haqqah 69:40-43

Yes. A person can be honest and mistaken. A good record speaks against fraud. It does not speak against error. What can be done is what any fair investigator does: list the possible explanations, and ask what each would lead you to expect. The people around this man did exactly that. They offered a poet, a soothsayer, a madman, someone taught by another, someone making it up. These lines answer two of those by name.

A question for you

If a sincere person were mistaken, where would you expect the mistake to show?

If you sayIn how the claim serves them.
ThenA mind that fools itself often does so in its own favour. That is what the next part looks at.
If you sayIn what they claim to know.
ThenThen look at the content, and whether it goes beyond what the person had access to. The part after that turns to it.
If you sayIt might not show at all.
ThenThat is possible, and it is the honest limit of this whole Step. Some errors leave no mark.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِى مَا يُفْعَلُ بِى وَلَا بِكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I am not something new among the messengers,[1479] nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."

Translator's notes

[1479] i.e., I am neither the first messenger to be sent, nor do I bring something different from the other messengers.

Quran · Al-Ahqaf 46:9

﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟ وَتَعْلَمَ ٱلْكَـٰذِبِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh has pardoned you, [O Muḥammad, but] why did you give them permission [to remain behind]? [You should not have] until it was evident to you who were truthful and you knew [who were] the liars.

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:43

A mind that is fooling itself tends to serve itself. It confirms what it wants and makes its owner the hero. So ask: does the message flatter the man who brings it? In this sentence he declares he does not know what will be done with him or his hearers. Elsewhere the same book questions a decision of his. This does not prove the source, and the objection stands: people do reproach themselves, sincerely or as a style. But any explanation has to fit it.

A question for you

What do those lines do for you as evidence?

If you sayThey count for something.
ThenThen they go on the scale, at their own weight. A single item decides nothing.
If you sayLittle. People criticise themselves.
ThenThat is the fair objection, and it stands. The next part looks elsewhere.
If you sayI would want to read them in context first.
ThenThat is what any text deserves.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا ۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِى مَا ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ وَلَا ٱلْإِيمَـٰنُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَـٰهُ نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِىٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command [i.e., the Qur’ān]. You did not know what is the Book or [what is] faith, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, [O Muḥammad], you guide to a straight path -

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:52

Translation

He led them also by a straight way, that they might go to a city to live in.

Original · Hebrew

וַ֭יַּֽדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃

the Psalms · 107:7

World English Bible

﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهَآ إِلَيْكَ ۖ مَا كُنتَ تَعْلَمُهَآ أَنتَ وَلَا قَوْمُكَ مِن قَبْلِ هَـٰذَا ۖ فَٱصْبِرْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلْعَـٰقِبَةَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muḥammad]. You knew it not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.

Quran · Hud 11:49

The other place a mistake would show is the content. A sincere person's visions are built from what they already carry. So ask what this man carried, and whether it accounts for what came. The book says that he and his people did not know certain accounts. A critic replies that stories of this kind circulated around him. So this cannot stand as a proof by itself. The form that holds is narrower: the book says this openly, before people who could have answered it.

A question for you

Which explanations are still on your list?

If you sayA sincere man, mistaken.
ThenThat is the strongest alternative, and it has been left standing here. What it has to account for is the whole: the man, the message and what came of it.
If you sayA sincere man, and something real behind it.
ThenThen you have gone further than this Step asks, and the question becomes what that real thing was.
If you sayI don't know. I cannot decide this.
ThenThat is a fair place to be, and no one here needs you to move.

The same in the other books

Translation

Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

Original · Hebrew

נֵר־לְרַגְלִ֥י דְבָרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝א֗וֹר לִנְתִיבָתִֽי׃

the Psalms · 119:105

World English Bible

Your reflection

What do you hold with full sincerity, and how would you find out if you were mistaken?
